title: User Acceptance of “Wider Web” in Autistic Adults: A Neurodiversity‐Informed Multifeature Browser Extension
abstract: Research examining technology acceptance among autistic populations remains limited, with existing work focusing primarily on mobile applications, augmentative and alternative communication systems, and educational software rather than web extensions. To our knowledge, no published study has applied technology acceptance constructs to evaluate browser extensions specifically designed for autistic users. This study examined user acceptability of Wider Web (by E&), a free multifeature browser extension developed in the UAE with input from autistic individuals and informed by accessibility principles. Wider Web provides eight accessibility features, including personalized color palettes and fonts, customizable webpage layouts, a timer, standardized icons, hover‐based visual focus support, and controls to disable advertisements and video autoplay. A structured questionnaire informed by core and extended constructs of the technology acceptance model (TAM) was administered to an international sample of 160 autistic adults (M = 31 years). Analyses were descriptive and exploratory rather than a formal structural test of TAM relationships. Participants generally reported positive perceptions of Wider Web across multiple acceptance dimensions. Wider Web was viewed as particularly supportive for learning, studying, work‐related activities, and online communication while also helping create a more structured and predictable browsing experience. Seven of its eight individual features were rated as significantly useful, with disabling video autoplay and pop‐up advertisements receiving the highest ratings. Lower agreement was observed for feature clarity and entertainment‐related usefulness. Overall, the findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the acceptability of Wider Web among autistic users and highlight implications for technology acceptance research within disability and neurodiversity contexts.
